newsitem.title: UK: CWS to contact UK SFO if query not answered.
newsitem.headline: CWS to contact UK SFO if query not answered.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society chief Graham Melmoth has told Andrew Regan, who is attempting to bid for the mutually-owned group, he will contact the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) if Regan does not provide answers to questions about a two million pound ($3.3 million) payment by Tuesday.

In a letter sent by fax to Regan on Monday, Melmoth asked him to clarify the role of a company called Trellis, why he was willing to pay "in excess of two million pounds for it" and who at the CWS was told of the payment, which related to the purchase by Regan of a CWS food manufacturing arm in May 1994.

"These are simple and straight-forward questions which call for simple and straight-forward answers. If these do not reach us by the close of business tomorrow, arrangements will be made to see representatives of the Serious Fraud Office (SFO)," Melmoth said in the letter.

In another letter last week to Lord Hambro, chairman of Hambros which is advising Regan's bidding vehicle Galileo, Melmoth said he had written to Regan asking about Trellis' involvement in the negotiations for the extension of a supply agreement between CWS and its former food manufacturning group.

He also said he had asked Regan if any third parties had been involved in the talks, why it was felt an intermediary was needed, the size of the payment to Trellis and whether there were any circumstances which would cause Regan to believe any part of the payment would benefit any other person.

Melmoth's latest move is yet another twist to an unusual takeover saga, which has already seen Regan's bid temporarily thwarted by CWS legal action, the suspension of two senior CWS managers for alleged serious breach of trust and the revelation that the CWS hired private investigators to trail Regan and others.
